title: U.S. House · Florida's 12th District
area: West-central Florida in the Tampa Bay area, including parts of Pinellas and Hillsborough counties.

context.text: The Republican primary was canceled and incumbent Gus Bilirakis advanced unopposed. Kimberly Overman won the Democratic primary against Darren McAuley.

candidates.name: Gus Bilirakis

summary.text: Gus Bilirakis is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election to Florida's 12th Congressional District. A lawyer by training, he owned an estate-planning law practice before his election to Congress.

background.text: Born in Gainesville, Florida; earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Florida (1986) and a law degree from Stetson Law School (1989).
Owned a law practice focused on estate planning and served on the board of Lighthouse for the Blind, the Rotary Club, and his local chamber of commerce before entering Congress.

record.text: Assigned to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, chairing its Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade Subcommittee, and to the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, for the 2025-2026 Congress.

candidates.researchNotes: Bilirakis has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; no additional sourced statements of current priorities or issue positions were found in the time available.

summary.text: Kimberly Overman is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 12th Congressional District. A former Hillsborough County Commissioner, small-business owner, and retired financial advisor, she is running on lowering costs, protecting healthcare, and government accountability.

background.text: Spent more than 30 years as a financial advisor helping families with financial planning before retiring.
Served as a Hillsborough County Commissioner, where she says she built a record on fiscal responsibility, transparency, and balanced budgets.
Says she is raising her grandson after caring for her adult son following a traumatic brain injury until his death in 2023.

priorities.text: Lowering costs for families, including healthcare, prescription drug, housing, and insurance costs.
Protecting access to healthcare and strengthening Social Security and Medicare, and supporting caregivers.
Restoring trust in government through transparency and accountability.

positions.summary: Says she will protect access to healthcare and strengthen Social Security and Medicare.

candidates.name: Branden Scrivener

summary.text: Branden Scrivener is running with no party affiliation for Florida's 12th Congressional District in the November 3, 2026 general election.
